titre_page: How to move a character in Yop2D? | Yop2D Guide
description: Three simple ways to move a character in Yop2D, without code: on-screen buttons, virtual joystick, or dragging with your finger.
carte: Move an object with buttons, the joystick or your finger.
etapes: Link the {{NoeudEventMaintenuObjet}} event of each button to a {{pousser}} node with {{lang:pousser.x}} = -5 or 5.
Add a {{lang:obj_prefix_joystick}} object and choose the character in {{lang:insp_label_cible_joystick}}. No node needed.
By dragging it with your finger
blocs: In Yop2D, there are three simple ways to move a character, without writing code. Pick the one that fits your game.
Great for a platform game, or a game where the character moves along a line.
In your scene, add your character (a **{{lang:obj_prefix_carre}}** or an **{{lang:obj_prefix_image}}**) and name it **player**.
Add two objects to use as buttons, for example two **{{lang:obj_prefix_bouton}}** objects (or two squares) named **btnLeft** and **btnRight**. Put them at the bottom of the screen.
Add the **[[NoeudEventMaintenuObjet]]** event and choose **btnLeft** as its target.
Link the event's output to the input of [[pousser]].
Save, then start the game: as long as your finger stays on a button, the character moves.
[[NoeudEventMaintenuObjet]] repeats on every frame while the finger stays on the button: that is why the character keeps moving. To go faster, raise the value (for example 8 or 10).
Great for a top-down game, where the character moves in every direction. **No node needed.**
Add a **{{lang:obj_prefix_joystick}}** object to your scene (category **{{lang:cat_interactifs}}**) and put it at the bottom left.
Select the joystick. In the inspector, section **[[lang:insp_sep_joystick]]**, tap the **[[lang:insp_label_cible_joystick]]** button and choose your character.
Save, then start the game: the character follows the joystick.

**Shortcut:** if you give your character the tag **Player** (or **Joueur**), the joystick moves it automatically, even if nothing is chosen in [[lang:insp_label_cible_joystick]]. Careful: this tag wins over the inspector's choice.

**Going further:** the formulas `joystick.x` and `joystick.y` give the direction (between -1 and 1). You can use them in a [[pousser]] node linked to [[NoeudEventChaqueImage]], for example `=joystick.x * 5`. The **[[si_joystick]]** node also has {{lang:port_haut}}, {{lang:port_bas}}, {{lang:port_gauche}}, {{lang:port_droite}} and {{lang:port_repos}} outputs.
Method 3: drag it with your finger
Great for a puzzle, a card game or any game where you move pieces around.
Select your object in the scene editor.
Start the game: you can drag the object with your finger.
To react when the player lets go of the object (for example to check it is in the right place), use the **[[NoeudEventFinGlisser]]** event.
To allow or block dragging during the game (a puzzle piece in the right place, for example), use the **[[modifier_deplacable]]** node.
**To make the character jump**, follow the guide [Make a character jump](guide:sauter).
**The « Platform » example game** that comes with Yop2D uses method 1: open it to see a complete Blueprint that works.
